title: Centralize standard formats in lib/format
description:
apps/web/src/lib/format.ts exports exactly one helper (formatDate, Intl-based) and is imported by zero product surfaces -- its only consumers are components/ui/notification-card.tsx and components/ui/table/data-table-date-filter.tsx. Everything else re-derives formatting locally.

formatTimestamp is copy-pasted into SEVEN components, byte-identical modulo the format string:
- features/market/components/items-table.tsx:27-29
- features/market/components/monitors-table.tsx:33-35
- features/market/components/search-dashboard.tsx:19-21
- features/market/components/item-state-card.tsx:10-12
- features/settings/components/connections-table.tsx:58-60
- features/settings/components/ebay-connection-actions.tsx:14-16
- features/settings/components/notification-deliveries-table.tsx:25-27

Five distinct format strings ship for the same concept: 'yyyy-MM-dd' (users-table.tsx:123), 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm', 'yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss' (opportunities-table.tsx:21, event-history-list.tsx:35, recent-events-list.tsx:39), 'MM/dd HH:mm' (chart axes), 'PPpp' (chart tooltips). Plus a raw ISO string leaked into a page subtitle at routes/market/items/$itemId.tsx:48 (renders as 2026-08-11T04:23:17.882Z). All call new Date(value) unguarded, so a malformed timestamp yields "Invalid Date" in a table cell; lib/format.ts has the try/catch they lack. Null sentinel is inconsistent too ('--' in the helpers, '' at users-table.tsx:49).

Money is the most consequential finding. formatPrice is duplicated verbatim at features/market/components/items-table.tsx:31-34 and item-state-card.tsx:14-17, and does naive string concat: `${price} ${currency}`. The DB decimal string ships raw, so "1250.00" + "USD" renders as `1250.00 USD` -- no symbol, no thousands separator, currency trailing against en-US convention, currency nullable so a price can render as a bare unlabeled number, no decimal normalization ("12.5" and "12.50" in adjacent rows), no tabular-nums, no right alignment.

Same-quantity precision drift: opportunity score is toFixed(4) at opportunities-table.tsx:120 and toFixed(2) at routes/market/overview.tsx:69, so the same score renders as 0.8734 on one route and 0.87 on another.

Hand-rolled durations: availability-timeline.tsx:25-30 formatSeconds (m/h/d), features/settings/components/health-report.tsx:17-23 formatUptime (s/m/h) -- two different implementations of the same idea, neither exported. monitors-table.tsx:143-145 renders the same concept as raw concat `${monitor.intervalSeconds}s`, so a 3600s interval shows as "3600s" not "1h". date-fns intervalToDuration is already a dependency and is imported in the very file that reimplements it.

Other inline formatting: item-state-card.tsx:100 priceChangePct.toFixed(2) + '%' with no sign; storage-backends-table.tsx:23-35 describeConfig manual concat; application-settings.tsx:23-27 formatValue via JSON.stringify; connections-table.tsx:319-321 composes two facts into one cell string; integrations-catalog.ts:95-97 and :208 duplicate ad-hoc pluralization.

Build out lib/format.ts with: formatDateTime, formatTimestampPrecise, formatRelativeTime (Intl.RelativeTimeFormat, paired with an absolute value in a title attribute), formatMoney(amount: string, currency: string | null) built on Intl.NumberFormat and fed from the decimal string -- money is PostgreSQL numeric and must never round-trip through JS number -- formatQuantity, formatPercent (explicit sign), formatDuration, formatScore, and move/re-export formatBytes from lib/utils.ts:21. Then delete every local copy. date-fns stays, but only inside lib/format.

The one correct precedent to preserve: price-history-chart.tsx:32 does Number(bucket.lastPrice) with a comment (L21-26) explaining it is chart-axis-only and never for stored or compared amounts.
acceptance_criteria: No component outside lib/format imports date-fns. Zero local formatTimestamp/formatPrice/formatSeconds/formatUptime copies. formatMoney renders decimal strings via Intl.NumberFormat with no JS number arithmetic. One precision per quantity across routes. Null renders as an em dash from the helper.

title: Status and health tone: add success/warning tokens, map state to tone
description:
19 of 24 badges across settings and market are variant='outline'. A price_drop event and a listing_ended event are visually indistinguishable; a monitor with 47 consecutive failures reads the same as one with 0.

Root cause: components/ui/badge.tsx:11-20 defines only default | secondary | destructive | outline | ghost | link, and no theme file defines --success or --warning. So "healthy" has no tone to reach for and degrades to neutral grey, while every non-healthy state is either full alarm red or neutral.

Work:
1. Add --success / --success-foreground and --warning / --warning-foreground to all ten theme files under apps/web/src/styles/themes/*.css (light and .dark blocks), wire them into each file's @theme inline block, and add matching Badge/Alert variants. Keep mono and notebook achromatic-consistent -- meaning must never be carried by hue alone, so pair every tone with an icon.
2. Replace the four independent, duplicated status->variant mappers with per-feature maps that use the new tones:
   - features/settings/components/settings-page.tsx:30-41 StatusBadge (ok ? 'secondary' : 'destructive'). Semantic overload: a *disabled* endpoint (operator choice) gets the same alarm red as a *failing* health check. Call sites: entities-table.tsx:143, storage-backends-table.tsx:105, notification-endpoints-table.tsx:117, notification-rules-table.tsx:127, health-report.tsx:54 and :110.
   - features/settings/components/connections-table.tsx:52-56 statusVariant
   - features/settings/components/notification-deliveries-table.tsx:19-23 statusVariant (near-identical duplicate of the above)
   - features/settings/components/integration-card.tsx:10-14 STATUS_VARIANT -- the clearest miss: IntegrationStatusTone already models 'ready' | 'partial' | 'unconfigured' (integrations-catalog.ts:34) and 'partial' ("Redirect URL name missing") is mapped to destructive because the design system cannot express a warning.
   - features/market/components/market-page.tsx:40 StatusBadge (ok ? 'secondary' : 'destructive'), used by monitors-table.tsx:141.
3. Untoned health signals to fix:
   - monitors-table.tsx:149-151 -- consecutiveErrors rendered as plain <TableCell className='text-muted-foreground'>. The single clearest health-signal miss in the audit.
   - items-table.tsx:136 -- <Badge variant='outline'>{item.currentState}</Badge>, raw enum, every state identical.
   - availability-timeline.tsx:64 -- in_stock ? 'secondary' : 'outline'; both branches neutral, so out-of-stock is LESS prominent than in-stock.
   - opportunities-table.tsx:117/:120 -- event type outline, score untoned.
   - item-state-card.tsx:100 -- priceChangePct with no sign and no tone: -40% and +40% render identically.
4. components/ui/badge.tsx:15 hardcodes text-white in the destructive variant. Replace with the token pair.

Also raise the token floor while here: features/settings uses 44x text-muted-foreground and ZERO primary/accent/chart-*; features/market uses 51x text-muted-foreground and one text-primary. Give each surface at least one emphasis token. Judge against a chromatic theme -- DEFAULT_THEME is 'vercel', which is itself near-monochrome.

One state->tone map per feature, no duplicates. consecutiveErrors, item state, availability and opportunity score all carry tone plus an icon. title: Add uniqueness and indexes to resource_links and media_links
description: Foundation defect found during Phase 6 design: 0000_auth_and_foundation.sql created resource_links and media_links with no PK, no unique constraint, and no index — an at-least-once integration job can double-link with no ON CONFLICT target. title: Wire search/seller executors into @loxep/app
description:
Phase 2 primitives for search rules, seller monitoring, and new-listing detection are implemented and tested in @loxep/integration-ebay and @loxep/market (loxep-7dp.1/.2), but NOTHING calls them: the poll executor in @loxep/app has no branch for the new target types. This issue is the wiring.

WHAT EXISTS ALREADY (do not rebuild):
- @loxep/integration-ebay: searchListings(adapter, {query?, categoryId?, filters?, sort?, limit?, cursor?}) and searchAllListings(adapter, {..., maxItems}) over Browse search; fetchSellerListings/fetchAllSellerListings(adapter, {sellerUsername, query?, categoryId?, filters?, sort?, limit?, cursor?, maxItems}) over the Browse 'sellers' filter. Both return normalized EbayListingSummary values plus total/offset/limit/cursor/warnings. Application token only (EbayAdapter, never EbayUserAdapter).
- @loxep/market: monitorTargetConfigSchemas.ebay_search / .ebay_seller; diffDiscoveredItems({knownExternalIds, fetchedSummaries}); knownExternalItemIds(db, {provider, marketplace, externalItemIds}); deriveNewListingEvents(db, {monitorTargetId, newlyLinkedItems, detectedAt?}).

WHAT THE EXECUTOR BRANCH MUST DO (per claimed target, target_type in ('ebay_search','ebay_seller')):
1. Mint ONE observationBatchId and fix observedAt at fetch time; both must survive retries (the observation write path keys on them).
2. Build the adapter from the target's connection; pass the connection's shared RateBudget. maxItems (config, default e.g. 200) bounds paging - each page spends budget.
3. ebay_search: searchAllListings(adapter, {query, categoryId, filters, sort: 'newlyListed', maxItems}). ebay_seller: fetchAllSellerListings(adapter, {sellerUsername, query, categoryId, filters, maxItems}). config.filters.listedAfter is an ISO STRING in jsonb; the adapter accepts Date|string, so it can be passed through unchanged.
4. BEFORE upserting anything, call knownExternalItemIds(db, {provider:'ebay', marketplace: adapter.marketplaceId, externalItemIds}) and diffDiscoveredItems(...). After the upsert every item looks known, so the order is load-bearing.
5. For every fetched summary: upsertMarketplaceItem (summary fields map 1:1 - externalItemId, title, price/currency, canonicalUrl, sellerExternalId, conditionCode, categoryExternalId, listingType, listingStartedAt, listingEndsAt) then linkItemToMonitor(db, {monitorTargetId, marketplaceItemId, at: observedAt}).
6. Record an observation batch for the page (search summaries carry no quantity/availability - leave those NULL, never 0).
7. Call deriveNewListingEvents(db, {monitorTargetId, newlyLinkedItems: <the diff's newItems, mapped to marketplaceItemId + payload facts>, detectedAt}) AFTER linking. It is idempotent and only fires on first GLOBAL discovery.
8. Report recordPollSuccess with changed = (newItems.length > 0 || any derived event), plus the rate-budget floor as bounds.minSeconds.
9. Inspect page.warnings: errorId 12002 means eBay IGNORED a filter and returned unfiltered results, 12008 means it ignored the sort. Log them; treat 12002 on a monitor as a configuration error rather than as discovery data. fetchSellerListings already THROWS on 12003 (unknown seller) rather than returning the anchor's whole result set.

GOTCHAS VERIFIED AGAINST THE LIVE SANDBOX (2026-08-11):
- eBay rejects a filter-only search with errorId 12001; a seller filter is NOT an anchor. Seller enumeration therefore defaults to EBAY_ROOT_CATEGORY_ID ('0'), which is undocumented but observed to work when paired with a valid seller filter.

OQ6's double-count guard is implemented at both fee scopes — any order_fees row referenced by a shipment's order_fee_id is excluded from the fee side, shipping comes from shipments only, and unlinkedShippingLabelFees() is the reconciliation report for the residual forgot-the-link risk. Where several items deplete one line the line's revenue/refunds/fees are split by depleted quantity, also largest-remainder — a step the design left to implementation, flagged PROVISIONAL and top of the reviewer pushback list. OQ8: mixed cost/sale currency yields contributionComputable:false with a null contribution and both figures shown, counted in excludedForeignCurrencyItemCount; nothing is converted. OQ9: consignment rows are returned and flagged, excluded from totals by an explicit source_kind predicate rather than by a zero. Reversed depletions are netted out so a cancelled sale is not counted. title: Order allocation and depletion
description: Allocate inventory lots to Phase 3 order lines; depletion on fulfillment; idempotent under re-ingestion. Docs closeout: affected docs surfaces updated and docs build green before close.
close_reason: Implemented PROVISIONALLY. packages/inventory/src/allocations.ts reserves against Phase 3 order_lines and depletes on fulfillment. Allocation is NOT a movement: a reservation writes nothing to inventory_movements, and available-to-sell is quantity_on_hand minus an indexed sum over open allocations, computed and never cached (the design's deliberate one-cache asymmetry). Reserve is idempotent per (order_line, item) while the hold is open, backed by the partial unique on status in ('reserved','fulfilled') — so a released hold does not block a later legitimate one. Over-allocation at reserve time IS rejected (a reservation is ours to refuse); allowOverAllocation exists for the operator who can see the stock and is off by default. Depletion consumes reserved allocations oldest-first, writes signed-negative depletion_sale movements keyed ffl:<fulfillment>:<line>:alloc:<allocation>, marks the allocation fulfilled only once the whole reservation is consumed (so one reservation split across two fulfillments stays open in between, with two distinct dedup keys), sets cost_basis_locked_at if null, and sets depleted_at at zero — all in one transaction. Idempotent under re-ingestion: a double-fired fulfillment depletes exactly once. The no-allocation branch NEVER raises — it returns unmatched:true and the line surfaces in the unmatchedDepletions read model, which is the design's central rule for this bead. Oversell is recorded and flagged, never blocked. Release/cancel/expire paths and a stale-manual-hold sweeper included. Tests: 13 in allocations.test.ts covering the full lifecycle, over-allocation refusal, release freeing the partial unique, refusal to release a fulfilled hold, the split across multiple items, the two-fulfillment partial consumption, the unmatched backlog, and ledger/cache agreement afterwards.

Nine designed tables: acquisitions, acquisition_costs, inventory_locations, inventory_items, inventory_allocations, inventory_movements, shipments, shipment_items, acquisition_opportunity_links. No existing table gains a column.

Load-bearing recommendations: (1) SPECIFIC IDENTIFICATION over FIFO for one-of-a-kind resale goods -- argued on non-fungibility, information already present at pick time, self-contradiction of per-item margin under an assumed cost flow, and decisively on reversibility (specific data can be re-reported as FIFO; FIFO data can never be re-reported specifically). No cost-layer table: an inventory_items row IS a layer, so FIFO is a picker policy (oldest acquired_at) selected by what the allocation identifies -- the exit path costs no migration. (2) Cost basis freezes at first depletion_sale; re-allocating an open lot redistributes only the unlocked remainder. (3) Entity attribution stored on BOTH acquisitions and inventory_items and IMMUTABLE; a change of owning entity is a paired transfer_out/transfer_in creating a new row, not an UPDATE -- preserving the Phase 3 write-once invariant while supporting personal-to-LLC contribution. (4) Movements are append-only with signed quantity and ONE location per row (a transfer is two rows sharing transfer_group_id), so on-hand and per-location balance stay a plain sum(); idempotency via deduplication_key reusing the market_events mechanism. (5) Allocation is NOT a movement -- reservations are intentions that may never happen.

OPEN QUESTIONS (10, each with a recommendation): 1 where a per-SKU costing policy would live (rec: none now; catalog_items.costing_method additively later, and that is Phase 3's document to amend, not this one). 2 append-only enforcement on inventory_movements (rec: BEFORE UPDATE OR DELETE trigger; a TypeScript-only rule is a convention, not an invariant). 3 cache quantity_on_hand vs derive from movements (rec: cache with nightly reconciliation; deriving is on every availability path while the ledger only grows). 4 location on the item row vs a per-location balance table (rec: single column, split-on-transfer; the balance table is additive). 5 when cost basis freezes (rec: first depletion; never-locking lets a March re-allocation rewrite February margin). 6 which record is authoritative for marketplace-purchased postage (rec: shipments authoritative, order_fees stays as ingested evidence, shipments.order_fee_id links them so the read model excludes the fee -- without this every per-item margin subtracts postage twice). 7 pro-rata basis for allocating order-scoped fees and shipping to lines, closing Phase 3 open question 1 (rec: by line_total net of line discounts, largest-remainder rounding, computed never stored). 8 mixed currency between cost basis and sale (rec: no conversion in Phase 4, consistent with Phase 3; report the gap honestly rather than store a rate). 9 consignment goods (rec: ordinary items with zero basis, excluded from profitability by explicit predicate not by the accident of a zero; an ownership column is where this ends up). 10 non-capitalized acquisition costs before Phase 5 exists (rec: keep them; the risk is a labeling problem, not a schema one).

14 OPEN QUESTIONS carry recommendations. Top 3 flagged OWNER-REVIEW-CRITICAL (unrecoverable after the first entry posts):

 3. Functional currency per book, effectively immutable -> conversion at posting with the rate frozen on the line; resolves Phase 3 OQ4 and Phase 4 OQ8; no FX revaluation policy.
Remaining 11: DB balance-enforcement mechanism (deferred constraint trigger; a deferred CHECK does not exist in PostgreSQL), soft-close states + who may backdate, signed amount vs debit/credit columns, entity-as-column vs generic dimension, unenforced source-fact stamps vs typed FKs, financial-account-to-ledger mapping across two books, facilitator-tax clearing treatment, bank-import dedupe identity, cash-basis support, closing entries/retained earnings, and package ownership across four finance domains.
